newsitem.title: USA: Police probe drug source in cult mass suicide.
newsitem.headline: Police probe drug source in cult mass suicide.

text.p: Police probing the mass suicide of 39 Heaven's Gate cult members focused on Saturday on finding out how the group managed to acquire massive amounts of phenobarbitol, the drug they used to kill themselves.

San Diego County Medical Examiner Dr. Brian Blackbourne said a lethal dose of the prescription sleeping pill amounted to 50 tablets for each person. To ensure death the cult members also put plastic bags over their heads secured by elastic bands.
Police said that while they did not expect any criminal charges to result from the mass suicide they were anxious to know how the cult got its hands on so much phenobarbitol.
"We're talking probably more than a thousand tablets here," one investigator said.
As autopsies were being carried out on the last of the victims, the first family to claim the body of a relative arrived in San Diego on Saturday from Canada, taking authorities by surprise.
Officials earlier had said they did not expect any families to come to San Diego and that arrangements were being made to ship the 39 bodies to the states where their relatives lived.
A man who gave his name as Ernst arrived at the San Diego morgue on Saturday morning and told reporters he had come to claim the body of his daughter. Among those listed as dead was Erika Ernst, 40.
The father was accompanied by his wife and sister and a second man and a teenage boy. The family arrived in two motor homes bearing Alberta license plates.
About two hours later they left with a police escort, but it was not clear if they took the woman's body.

San Diego County Sheriff's Dept. Sgt. Dan Wall said the family's arrival was "totally unexpected." He said the Ernsts were the only family to arrive and he did not anticipate any other families coming to San Diego.

Calvin Vine, an investigator with the San Diego County Coroner's office, said on Friday the funerals would take place in the states where the deceased had families. "We have actively discouraged (families) from coming here," he said.
He said that a local funeral home was coordinating the removal of the bodies to a number of states. The bodies were expected to be shipped out of San Diego on Monday.

All 39 members of the cult killed themselves over a period of days. According to their videotaped suicide notes, the cultists, who ran a successful business designing computer Web sites for the Internet, believed that a spaceship hiding behind the Hale-Bopp comet nearing Earth would take them to heaven.

Their bodies were discovered on Wednesday in the $1.6 million mansion the cult rented in the exclusive San Diego suburb of Rancho Santa Fe, but officials said the death ritual probably began last Saturday.

By Friday night, autopsies had been performed on 30 of the victims and on Saturday morning the medical examiner's office began autopsies on four more. Thirty-five of the victims' families had been notified.
Officials said on Friday that 18 male victims had been castrated and that one was the brother of 1960's "Star Trek" television series actress Nichelle Nichols, who played Lt. Uhura.
Thomas Nichols, 59, was one of two black members of the group. Two others were Hispanic and the rest were white.

In a videotaped suicide note aired on Friday, members of the group explained how their deaths were part of a greater plan to join with the space aliens they believed were following the comet Hale-Bopp to Earth. "We have no hesitation to leave this place, to leave the bodies that we have," charismatic cult leader Marshall Applewhite, one of those who died, said.
The Cincinnati Enquirer reported on Saturday that a local woman who died in the mass suicide left behind new-born twins and three other children when she joined the cult late last year.

The newspaper said Yvonne McCurdy-Hill, 38, a veteran U.S. Post Office worker, left her children with relatives when she became a cult member. Her husband, Steven, accompanied her to California but returned to the predominantly black suburb of Lincoln Heights a few weeks later.
